feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Trump's messaging meanders as GOP makes final push toward Election Day
entry.summary: President Trump crisscrosses the country with scattershot closing messages ahead of the midterm elections.

entry.title: Larry Sabato on Trump's messaging and the issues driving voters to the polls
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with political analyst Larry Sabato about President Trump's messaging and the issues likely to determine the outcome of the midterm elections.

entry.title: Tampa Bay Rays extends World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers
entry.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays won a thrilling 12-inning game to keep their World Series hopes alive. The Milwaukee Brewers have a 3-1 lead as the Series goes to Game 5.

entry.title: New teachers union president wants to steer educators away from partisan politics
entry.summary: NEA President Princess Moss wants to move her organization, the nation's largest labor union, toward issue-based advocacy — and away from party politics.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: President Trump crisscrosses the country with scattershot closing messages midterms approach, deadlock after Israeli election shows no clear winner, Fed expected to hold interest rates steady.

entry.title: For the first time in 40 years, Elton John lyricist Bernie Taupin is taking the mic
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with longtime Elton John lyricist Bernie Taupin {TAW-pin}, who's released his first solo album in 40 years, "The Sea Has No Mercy."

entry.title: Trump's relationship with Putin comes under fire ahead of the midterms
entry.summary: President Trump's relationship with Russia's Vladimir Putin is under scrutiny again as the president makes deals with Moscow ahead of the midterms.

entry.title: Former DOJ official on judge blocking Trump's D.C. golf course renovation
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with author and former Justice Department official Sarah Isgur about the block on President Trump's renovation of the East Potomac Golf Course.

entry.title: Iran war and cost-of-living take center stage in Virginia congressional race
entry.summary: High prices and long deployments are shaping this year's race in Virginia's Second Congressional District. The area with deep Navy ties has been a kind of political bellwether.

entry.title: Partial results from Israel's contentious election show no clear winner
entry.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was leading opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot. Arab parties had a strong showing, and a key question now is whether Eisenkot's bloc will consider forming a coalition with them.
